verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The change remains correct and complete under the adversarial trust-plane lens. All three routes select ALERT_REPO only after a token-scoped GET positively returns a literal boolean `private: true`; failed, raising, malformed, public, non-boolean, same-repository, and half-configured cases do not inherit private-route status. The standalone scripts fall back under the ambient registry credential, while worker-pr preserves its established registry-alert credential semantics and avoids propagating probe failures through the alerting path. The self-tests independently exercise the routing decisions, probe repository/token binding, no-probe short circuits, strict response parsing, and production alert-create wiring. I found no diff-supported correctness, security, injection, or test-vacuity issue requiring changes.
